name: Madison Mobile Solar, LLC
old_description: Add solar power, lithium batteries and many other upgrades to your RV, trailer, van or skoolie.
about:
Madison Mobile Solar, LLC is based in Fitchburg, Wisconsin, and operates a year-round installation shop at 8710- in Middleton. The company specializes in mobile solar and battery systems for recreational and commercial vehicles.

The business designs and builds complete electrical systems, handling everything from initial sizing and component selection to installation, programming, and customer training. It also troubleshoots and repairs underperforming setups and supports do-it-yourself projects with advice, key components, and programming assistance. As a certified Victron installer and an authorized dealer for Epoch Batteries and Rich Solar, the company stocks and supplies a range of inverters, charge controllers, lithium batteries, and solar panels.

Its customers include owners of RVs, trailers, vans, skoolies, and other mobile homes, as well as commercial vehicle operators seeking off-grid power solutions. The indoor shop allows work to continue through Wisconsin winters.

The company emphasizes safety compliance and customer education, teaching clients how to operate and manage their systems after installation.

name: Magcrest
old_description: Magcrest is a leading flexible packaging manufacturer specializing in custom retail bags, multi-layer films, and innovative packaging solutions.
about:
Magcrest was founded in 1991 in Monsey, New York, as a supplier of retail bags. The company quickly expanded into multi-layer films and a full range of flexible packaging. It operates offices in New York with warehouses in New Jersey and California, serving customers worldwide.

Magcrest manufactures custom retail bags, premade pouches, roll stock, shrink labels, sleeves, and merchandise bags. Its printing capabilities include flexographic, rotogravure, digital, and offset processes up to ten colors. The company works with a wide range of single- and multi-layer plastic films, papers, and sustainable materials such as compostable PLA and biodegradable PE. Annual output reaches tens of millions of packages, with order volumes ranging from a single carton to 1,000 tons.

The company serves the food, cosmetics, retail, and industrial sectors, providing packaging that enhances shelf life and brand presentation. Clients include brands seeking fully custom packaging solutions, from design consultation through prototyping to global delivery.

Magcrest differentiates itself with a responsive team that typically returns calls within ten minutes, lead times as short as two weeks, and the ability to combine plate and digital printing. Its global sourcing network spans ten countries, and the company emphasizes integrity by refusing to poach satisfied customers and taking full responsibility for every order.

The company manufactures pre-engineered steel buildings, premium metal panels, pole barns, and tube-frame carports. It handles every aspect of production in-house, maintaining direct control over quality and process efficiency. Facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not disclosed.

Magnum Metals serves residential, commercial, industrial, and structural customers across the Southeast. Its products are used in projects ranging from custom home metalwork to large-scale industrial fabrication.

The company distinguishes itself as the only Mississippi firm that manages all production stages internally, allowing complete oversight of quality and turnaround. This integrated approach is cited as the foundation of its reputation for reliability.

name: Magnum Truck Racks
old_description: If you see a 2025 or 2026 vehicle option, fitment is confirmed. If not, we are still working on confirming fitment.
about:
Magnum Truck Racks operates from Waterville, Maine, as a brand of the Aebi Schmidt Group. The company focuses on truck headache racks and accessories for pickup and service body trucks.

The product line spans headache racks in five model families—Low Pro, High Pro, Standard, Sport, and Service Body—along with bed rails, ladder racks, toolboxes, rear racks, wiring harnesses, and mounting accessories. All racks are built from aluminum and finished in matte black, mill finish, or satin white. The proprietary Glide Track system allows adjustable mounting without drilling. LED lighting packages integrate brake, backup, tail, and turn signals. Fitments cover model years from 2000 through 2026 for Chevrolet, Dodge, Ford, Jeep, GMC, Nissan, Ram, and Toyota trucks.

Customers include individual truck owners, commercial fleets, and upfitters who service body trucks. A dealer network extends across the U.S., and the company offers a 10 percent discount to military, police, and fire personnel. Orders over $100 ship free.

Magnum emphasizes lightweight strength, corrosion resistance, and installation flexibility as its core differentiators. The Glide Track system and vehicle-specific engineering aim to reduce install time and ensure a secure fit for each application.

name: Maine Adirondack Chairs, LLC
old_description: We are not able to control the metrics on the “Shop” page. We can't ship those items.
about:
Maine Adirondack Chairs, LLC operates from Vassalboro, Maine. The business traces its roots to 2012 when founder Rob transitioned from Grapevine Hill Woodworking to the current name after a suggestion from John Shaw. Rob remains involved while Nita now manages the shop and builds products, alongside Kate.

The company handcrafts outdoor furniture exclusively from Eastern White Cedar (Thuja occidentalis), planing and sanding only one face to yield thicker boards and reduce processing time. The small woodworking shop produces Adirondack chairs, rocking chairs, picnic tables, footstools, coffee tables, and campfire stools, with a capacity of roughly 30–40 chairs per week. Chairs are built then broken down into knock-down kits for shipping; smaller items such as footstools and coffee tables ship assembled.

Products serve both residential buyers and commercial settings—the “EZ‑UP” chair is designed for the rigors of commercial use. Customers order directly through the website, and the build‑to‑order model means inventory rarely sits on hand; high spring demand often leads to backorders by April.

The venture began almost by accident, driven by geographic economic pressures. After sparse demand for custom kitchen cabinets, Rob pivoted to Adirondack chairs, with most designs originating from customer requests and ergonomic experiments. The single‑side milling method and exclusive use of local white cedar keep prices reasonable while delivering rot‑resistant, decades‑long durability.

name: Maine Community Solar
old_description: Join Maine Community Solar and save 15% on your electric bill.
about:
Maine Community Solar operates from Portland, Maine, as a locally-owned company founded by Tony Napolitano. The firm was established to advance renewable energy adoption across the state by connecting residents and businesses with community solar programs.

The company provides enrollment assistance and education for community solar programs, helping customers subscribe to local solar farms without installing panels on their own properties. Its customer relations team guides clients through the signup process, which the company says takes about five minutes, and continues to provide support after enrollment. The firm reports assisting hundreds of Mainers in joining state community solar programs.

Clients include both residential and commercial customers. Restaurant groups, nonprofit organizations such as the Maine State Society for the Protection of Animals, and condominium residents who cannot install rooftop panels have all enrolled through the service. The company works with multiple solar farm developers to match customers with available capacity.

Napolitano frames the business as a mission-driven effort to make Maine a leader in sustainability. The company emphasizes honest communication, pressure-free enrollment, and ongoing customer support as distinguishing factors, with representatives often cited by name in customer testimonials for their responsiveness.

name: Maine Crisp Company
old_description: Our buckwheat crackers combine amazing taste with countless health benefits for the perfect go-to snack.
about:
Maine Crisp Company operates from Winslow, Maine, where founder Karen launched the business after a career that spanned bread baking, dairy farming, and cheesemaking. Unable to find gluten-free crackers that met her standards for ingredients, taste, and texture, she began developing her own buckwheat-based recipes. The company is now transitioning to the Better with Buckwheat brand.

The facility produces a line of gluten-free, grain-free crackers made from buckwheat, a seed cultivated for over 8,000 years. Current flavors include Cranberry Almond, Everything, Savory Fig & Thyme, and Sea Salt. Production is described as handmade, though the company does not disclose facility size, headcount, or annual volume.

Customers range from individual consumers to food-service accounts. Chefs at Union Restaurant in Portland and Alice and Lulu's in Sugarloaf Village have endorsed the crackers, as has C Salt Gourmet Market in Cape Elizabeth. The product is also sold direct through the company's website.

The company emphasizes buckwheat's environmental profile: it grows in low-fertility soils, regenerates the land, and supports pollinators—one acre can sustain a full hive. Nutritionally, the crackers are positioned as low-glycemic, anti-inflammatory, and high in fiber. Karen's original motivation was personal: creating a snack she could enjoy daily without compromising on flavor or ingredient integrity.

name: Maine Printing & Embroidery
old_description: Screen printing is at the ready with both manual and automatic equipment.
about:
Maine Printing & Embroidery operates from Warren, a coastal community in Maine's Mid Coast region. The family‑owned shop has been in business for more than 40 years, though a specific founding year is not published. The company began as a local screen printing and embroidery provider and has since expanded into a full‑service graphics and signage operation.

The facility houses both manual and automatic screen printing presses, enabling runs from a few custom tees to orders of several hundred pieces. In addition to screen printing, the shop offers embroidery, CAD‑cut vinyl graphics, banner and decal production, vehicle wraps, and general signage. An in‑house art department staffed with several artists handles original artwork, custom shirt designs, and vehicle‑wrap layouts, keeping all design and production under one roof.

The customer base includes businesses and organizations needing branded apparel, promotional items, fleet graphics, and interior or exterior signage. Small orders of just a couple of shirts are accommodated through vinyl cut graphics, while larger volumes move to screen printing. The shop also serves clients requiring vehicle identification, wall graphics, and business identification signage.

The company attributes its longevity to professionalism and quality, emphasizing that multiple services under one roof and an in‑house art team allow for prompt turnaround and consistent results. Family ownership remains a stated point of differentiation, with the owners highlighting personal service and direct communication.
